detail:

Explore stocks on Coinbase

Coinbase Global (Nasdaq: COIN) has Wall Street analysts moving in different directions on where the stock is headed, with price targets ranging from $187 to $280.

Founded by Brian Armstrong and Fred Ehrsam in 2012, Coinbase is the leading cryptocurrency trading exchange in the United States.

The firm went public in 2021 and joined the S&P 500 index in May 2025. It became the first pure-play crypto company to be a part of the much-coveted index.

Related: Coinbase CEO predicts 450% upside for Bitcoin

Letting users trade cryptocurrencies is just one function of Coinbase. It also lets them trade prediction markets and tokenized stocks and hold stablecoins.

In fact, stablecoins constitute a major part of the company's revenue stream. Coinbase distributes Circle Internet Group's (NYSE: CRCL) USDC stablecoin — a kind of digital dollar — to its users and generates revenue from the yields on the stablecoin's reserves, such as short-term U.S. Treasuries.

As the Federal Reserve raised the interest rates by 0.25% to the 3.75%-4.00% range last month, Bank of America recently raised its price target on the Coinbase stock from $174 to $203 and maintained a Buy rating.

The Wall Street bank expects the crypto company's stablecoin revenue to surge due to higher interest rates, prompting the price target hike.

Goldman Sachs raises Coinbase price target

On Oct. 7, Goldman Sachs raised its price target on the Coinbase stock while keeping a Buy rating.

The Wall Street giant said the crypto exchange could benefit from the U.S. Securities and Exchange Commission's (SEC) "innovation exemption."

Issued on Sep. 17, the order grants temporary, conditional exemptive relief to allow limited trading of tokenized stocks on Tokenized Securities Venues.

Goldman Sachs said Coinbase's stock's current price is "an attractive valuation entry point" for investors. The bank raised its price target from $219 to $244.

More on Coinbase:

Coinbase CEO has a bold take on the future of AI payments

Coinbase officer reveals new details on Bitcoin reserve bill

Coinbase's IPO move sends stock to four month high

Compass Point follows suit

On Oct. 7, Compass Point also raised its price target on the Coinbase stock from $177 to $187 while maintaining a Neutral rating.

The analyst's Q3 2026 earnings before interest, taxes, depreciation, and amortization (EBITDA) forecast stands 14% above consensus estimates. Coinbase posted EBITDA of $699.55 million over the last twelve months while maintaining an impressive gross profit margin of 85.81%.

title: Warren Buffett warns of a reality check coming for stock investors
detail:
Warren Buffett warns of a reality check coming for stock investors
Hillary Remy, Celine Provini
Sat, October 10, 2026 at 10:34 AM MST 5 min read
^GSPC
^IXIC
BRK-B

The S&P 500 is up roughly 19% over the past six months. The Nasdaq has gained about 26% over the same period. Both indexes hit record highs this week.

Those numbers look good on paper. The mood behind them is a different story. Price gains that outrun earnings attract a certain kind of buyer. History has a record of how that ends.

Warren Buffett has a name for what he is watching. He compared the current market to a church with a casino attached, and he was not flattering the casino side.

Also read: Warren Buffett doubles down on stock market message for 2026

What Buffett said and what he meant by the casino

Buffett made the remark during a CNBC interview at Berkshire Hathaway's annual meeting. The church, in his analogy, represents long-term investors buying businesses based on what they are actually worth. The casino is the other side, where rising prices, rather than the value underneath, drive the buying.

"We've never had people in a more gambling mood than now," Buffett told CNBC.

He added that this does not mean "investing is terrible," but that "prices for an awful lot of things will look very silly." That is a warning from someone who has watched markets for more than seven decades.

The number that shows how expensive stocks really are

One figure puts the current market in context. The S&P 500 Shiller CAPE ratio has been above 40 since May 2026. The ratio measures the index's price against its average inflation-adjusted earnings over the prior 10 years. A higher number means investors are paying more per dollar of earnings.

The long-term average sits at approximately 17. The ratio hit a record 44 in late 1999, shortly before the dot-com bubble burst in March 2000. The current reading does not guarantee a crash. It does mean that stocks are priced at levels that have historically left very little room for disappointment.

Buffett has repeated this warning throughout 2026. Berkshire Hathaway has also been sitting on cash rather than putting it to work. That is its own signal.

Buffett has repeated his warning that rising prices, rather than the value underneath, have driven the buying throughout 2026.Bloomberg / Getty Images
The 1990s already showed where this tends to go

The dot-com era is the closest modern comparison. Hundreds of technology companies saw their shares climb through the 1990s on enthusiasm alone. Many collapsed when the bubble burst in early 2000, and the worst performers were companies with weak balance sheets, unsustainable models, and little behind the stock price besides a rising chart.

The companies that held up were the ones with real earnings, manageable debt, and competitive advantages that were hard to copy. A rising stock price made a lot of businesses look successful. It did not keep them alive when sentiment turned.

title: Dell (DELL) Has Outpaced the S&P 500 by a Wide Stretch. Will the AI-Fueled Run Continue?
detail:
Dell (DELL) Has Outpaced the S&P 500 by a Wide Stretch. Will the AI-Fueled Run Continue?
Muhammad Ali
Sat, October 10, 2026 at 10:40 AM MST 4 min read
DELL
^GSPC
Trade DELL on Coinbase
Trading disclosure

Much of the recent growth for Dell Technologies Inc. (NYSE:DELL) has come through hardware sales, which is a lower-margin, high-volume avenue for the overall business. Bottom-line expansion in the future now hinges on diversification of its business mix and the underlying execution. The stock has gained 225.83% over the last six months, compared to a 33.88% for Insider Monkey Billionaire Index and 18.18% for S&P 500 ETF (SPY).

The company delivered a record-breaking second quarter print for fiscal 2027, largely driven by robust AI infrastructure demand. Topline jumped 58% year-over-year to $47 billion, as revenues for AI-optimized servers doubled to $16.4 billion. With Dell operating at such great scale, Jim Cramer continues to be a big fan of the stock.

Dell (DELL) Has Outpaced the S&P 500 by a Wide Stretch. Will the AI-Fueled Run Continue?

Sergiy Palamarchuk/Shutterstock.com

A Large-Cap Rally That Few Saw Coming

Dell closed at $578.96 on October 7, which extends one of the most notable runs across the large-cap tech universe. It is up almost 360% in 2026 and has massively outpaced the broader S&P 500 index over the same period. The fundamentals explain the ongoing bullish momentum. The company has generated $151.2 billion in cumulative revenue over the trailing twelve months, following the 57.7% growth in the last quarter.

Such growth is striking for a hardware-heavy business operating at this scale, and suggests demand is accelerating rather than merely recovering. But Dell is not the only name that is benefitting from AI. It will be interesting to see how the ongoing AI buildout positions this other memory and storage mega-cap stock to reward investors?

Credit Investors Are Also Noticing

What is interesting is that public market participants aren't the only investors attracted to Dell. The company is garnering attention from credit market investors too. In September, Dell's investment-grade bond sale was massively oversubscribed. The company had initially targeted $4 billion proceeds. However, the offering had to be upsized to $5 billion amid strong investor demand attributed to the company's booming AI server business.

What is more compelling is that investors are not giving too much consideration to the profitability metrics which are healthy but not extraordinary. Over the last 12 months, the company posted approximately 9.4% trailing operating margin along with net margin of 7.52%. These figures point to a sound hardware manufacturing business, but remain well below the typical range for software or chip companies. This makes investors wonder how is Dell positioned compare to HP in current landscape?

The S&P 500 (SNPINDEX: ^GSPC) recently hit a new high, building on its 78% returns over the past five years. The Dow Jones Industrial Average (DJINDICES: ^DJI) and the Nasdaq Composite (NASDAQINDEX: ^IXIC) have seen impressive returns over this period too, rising 48% and 88%.

Bull markets tend to last about five or six years, on average, and the current one is already in its fourth year, which means that a bear market will show up eventually.

Missed AI's "Act 1"? Act 2 Could Be 14x Bigger. Most investors think they missed the AI boat because they didn't buy Nvidia in 2005. But according to our analysts, we're only at the end of "Act 1"—the R&D phase. "Act 2" is the global rollout. Continue »

So, what's the best way to prepare for one? You probably already know the answer, since it's a time-tested strategy for buying stocks: diversify.

One of the easiest ways to ensure your portfolio is instantly diversified is to buy an exchange-traded fund (ETF) with broad exposure to many stocks. And one of the best ones to own is the Vanguard Morningstar Total Stock Market ETF (NYSEMKT: VTI). Here's why it's worth buying now.

Image source: Getty Images.
Diversify your portfolio with a good exchange-traded fund

Diversifying your portfolio can be hard when a bull market is underway. For example, selling booming artificial intelligence (AI) stocks right now could result in you leaving a lot of money on the table.

What's great about owning the Vanguard Morningstar Total Stock Market ETF is that your portfolio has exposure to all areas of the market -- technology, industrials, consumer goods, energy, etc. -- and across a wide range of companies.

This Vanguard ETF tracks about 3,500 stocks spread across 11 sectors of the U.S. economy, including everything from large-cap tech companies like Nvidia to small-cap consumer goods companies, including Crocs.

This broad diversification is important because during a bear market, you never know which companies will fall the furthest or rebound the fastest.

You can't avoid bear markets

Unfortunately, there's no avoiding a bear market. The only thing you can be sure of is that there will be significant declines, especially considering that the average bear market downturn results in a 38% drop and typically lasts about 15 months.

Owning the Vanguard Morningstar Total Stock Market ETF won't shield you from the bear market's declines, but it will spread your risk around. And the added benefit of owning this Vanguard ETF during a bear market is that you won't miss out on the market's eventual rebound.
